solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Unfashionable garments for the suburbs? (9)

annotation.surface: A fashion verdict on what people wear out in the suburbs.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: dated skirts are literally 'out skirts', which is also where the suburbs lie.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the outskirts of a town are its outlying districts, its suburbs.

entries.clue: Manual worker producing notes in church? (8)

annotation.definition: Manual worker producing notes in church?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a labourer; the setter's reading: someone who plays a manual, an organ keyboard
not memos but musical notes, sounding in a church

annotation.surface: A labourer writing memos in church.
annotation.walkthrough: A manual is one of an organ's keyboards, played by hand; 'manual worker' reads as a labourer until the notes turn out to be music.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic definition: the church musician works the manuals by hand and produces notes.

entries.clue: Heavyweight head dismissed from school in Berkshire (3)

indicatorNotes.head dismissed: the head, first letter, is sent away

annotation.surface: A heavyweight headmaster sacked from a Berkshire school.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head dismissed' reads as a headteacher being fired, which suits the school setting; here it just drops the E. Berkshire is an English county west of London.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose sense: a unit of weight, used informally for anything very heavy.

entries.clue: Genuflect, hearing Lord Kinnock’s name? (5)

indicatorNotes.hearing: on hearing the name, go by its sound

annotation.surface: Someone dropping to one knee when a peer's name is announced.
annotation.walkthrough: Neil Kinnock was leader of the British Labour Party and now sits in the House of Lords; the silent K makes the sound match.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to genuflect is to bend one knee to the ground in reverence.

entries.clue: New order ran greater men ragged (13)

indicatorNotes.ragged: the letters are torn apart and put back together

annotation.surface: A new regime that ran its superiors ragged.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ran ... ragged' reads as a single idiom for wearing someone out, which hides 'ragged' as the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: putting things in a different sequence gives them a new order.

entries.clue: Sons mostly disregard a married woman in Rome (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, dropping its last letter

annotation.surface: Grown sons ignoring a woman in Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' sits after 'Sons' and seems to belong to it, but it trims the next word.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign word: the Italian title for a married woman, the equivalent of Mrs, as used in Rome.

entries.clue: Reduced share of profits? (3)

blocks.note: made smaller, as prices are in a sale
informal: a person's slice of the takings

annotation.surface: A partner grumbling that their slice of the business has shrunk.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, a smaller share, but it splits into two separate meanings of one short word.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the past participle of the verb to cut, meaning lowered, and the informal noun for a portion of the proceeds.

entries.clue: Woodwork in vehicle parking on arrival (9)

annotation.surface: Someone finding woodwork inside a car parked on arrival.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' just places ENTRY after the parking; 'in' links the definition to the wordplay rather than containing anything.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the craft of making things from wood.

entries.clue: River in remote estate (4)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A river running through an isolated country estate.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two words; the Tees is a river in north-east England.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Tees is one particular river.

entries.clue: Artilleryman introducing a herbaceous plant (7)

indicatorNotes.introducing: GUNNER comes first and so introduces the A that follows

blocks.note: a soldier who fires the big guns

annotation.surface: A soldier presenting a plant, as if at a garden show.
annotation.walkthrough: Gunnera is the giant-leaved plant sometimes called giant rhubarb, grown beside ponds in large gardens.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by genus: Gunnera is a genus of large herbaceous plants.

entries.clue: Turn right, initially seeing evergreen shrub (5)

indicatorNotes.initially: take the initial letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: your go = your turn in a game
first letters of Seeing and Evergreen

annotation.surface: Driving directions: turn right when you spot a particular evergreen bush.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen shrub' wants to be the definition, and fits; but 'evergreen' is needed for its E, so the definition is just 'shrub'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: gorse, or furze, is a spiny yellow-flowered shrub of heaths.

entries.clue: Coward, possibly, digesting beginning of Victorian literary work (5)

indicatorNotes.possibly: Coward is only one example of a man called Noel, so the name is a definition by example
indicatorNotes.digesting: NOEL swallows the V, holding it inside
indicatorNotes.beginning of: take the first letter of Victorian

annotation.surface: Noel Coward taking in a Victorian book.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coward' reads as a timid person; the capital C is the only hint that it is Noel Coward, the English playwright and wit.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a novel is one kind of literary work, a long prose fiction.

entries.clue: Practicality little Violet put before skill (9)

indicatorNotes.put before: VI is placed in front of ABILITY

blocks.note: the short form of the name

annotation.surface: A practical-minded parent putting a young girl ahead of talent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals a shortened name, not a small girl.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: whether a plan can actually work is its feasibility or practicality.

entries.clue: Rampager in Brazilian port starts to terrorise edgy residents (6)

indicatorNotes.starts to: take the starting letter of each of the following words

blocks.note: first letters of Terrorise, Edgy, Residents

annotation.surface: A marauder loose in a Brazilian city, frightening nervous locals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rampager in' reads as the rampager being located in the port; 'in' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who runs amok in a violent crowd is on the rampage.

entries.clue: Campaigner from South Africa in simpler setting (8)

indicatorNotes.in: in, meaning placed within: South Africa's letters sit within the word for simpler
indicatorNotes.setting: the word for simpler is the setting that holds it

annotation.surface: An activist from South Africa operating in a plainer environment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'From' reads as the campaigner's homeland, but it only links the definition to the wordplay; 'setting' is a jewellery image for the outer word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who campaigns hard for a cause is on a crusade.

entries.clue: Railway employee adjusting to steam trains (13)

indicatorNotes.adjusting: the letters are adjusted into a new order

annotation.surface: A railwayman converting engines to run on steam.
annotation.walkthrough: The fodder stays entirely on the railway theme, so the surface and the answer share one scene and the anagram hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the person in charge of a station is one kind of railway employee.

entries.clue: At home juggling dates as an alternative (7)

indicatorNotes.juggling: the letters of DATES are tossed about into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone staying in to juggle appointments as a fallback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Juggling' sits between the two chunks and belongs to the second; 'dates' reads as appointments but only supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adverb meaning in place of something else.

entries.clue: Absorbent paper he removed from the children (6)

indicatorNotes.removed from: HE is taken out of the phrase that follows

blocks.note: issue = offspring, children, in its legal sense
the letters H and E come out of the front word

annotation.surface: A father kept away from his children, with only paper left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The' is part of the fodder: HE comes out of it, leaving only its T in front of ISSUE, an old legal word for children.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: soft paper used for mopping up, as in a box of tissues.

entries.clue: Ravine originally accessed on ship (5)

indicatorNotes.originally: take the original, first letter of accessed

blocks.note: on = by, beside, as a town on the coast is by the sea

annotation.surface: A gorge first reached by boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is a small word doing real work: it means beside, as in a house on the river.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: an abyss is a deep chasm, and a ravine is a deep narrow gorge.

entries.clue: Top-grade hotel in mountain area (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in, meaning located within: the hotel sits inside mountain plus area, as a real hotel stands in the mountains

blocks.note: a high peak, especially in Switzerland
H = hotel, as in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A five-star hotel in the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: The hotel goes between the mountain and the area; in British marking an alpha is a top mark, as in alpha plus.
annotation.definitionFit: A marking convention: the first Greek letter stands for the best grade.

entries.clue: Ship’s company uttered exultant cries (4)

blocks.note: the people who work a ship
an old past tense of crow, to cry in triumph

annotation.surface: Sailors cheering in triumph.
annotation.walkthrough: The second meaning relies on the old past tense of crow, as in 'the cock crew', rarer today than crowed.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the collective noun for a ship's hands, and an archaic past tense of the verb to crow.

entries.clue: Put up beams, reportedly (5)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: what is reported is heard, not seen, so go by the sound

annotation.surface: A builder said to have fitted the roof timbers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beams' reads as timbers going up in a building, which suits 'put up', but it means shafts of light.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lift or erect something, as you put up a flag.

entries.clue: Old flame worked as model — with nothing on? (7)

annotation.surface: A former lover who once modelled in the nude.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end and doubles as the punchline of the story the surface tells.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to be wearing nothing is to be uncovered, open to view.

entries.clue: Determined group (3)

blocks.note: a collection of things or people that belong together

annotation.walkthrough: 'Determined group' reads as one resolute gang; split it into an adjective and a noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the adjective meaning resolved or fixed, and the noun for a collection.

entries.clue: Twisted grass, by the sound of it (3)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: go by how the word sounds

blocks.note: a cereal grass grown for grain and whisky

annotation.surface: A remark about grass that has been twisted.
annotation.walkthrough: The word sounds identical to the grain; spelt with a W it becomes the adjective.
annotation.definitionFit: An older sense: wry first meant bent or contorted, as in a wry neck, before it meant drily ironic.

entries.clue: Denigrator of French farm vehicle (9)

annotation.surface: Someone who runs down French farm machinery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of French' reads as describing the vehicle, but it asks for the French word for 'of'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are people who belittle or run others down.
